## (b) Decision heuristics (D1-D6)

**D1 (what to test next)**
- Test the model's ability to infer it is being tested or unmonitored, since this undermines every other evaluation. 
  > "If a model is situationally aware, it’s harder to test whether it is aligned or safe. Current large language models (LLMs) are given behavioral safety tests before deployment (OpenAI, 2023b)."  
  > -- `research__paper_on_measuring_situational_awareness_in_llms_5b02029a` (2023-09-04; first author) 
  > "You could make it believe that its chain of thought is never monitored and also believe that if it tries to reason about whether its chain of thought is monitored, then it will fail"  
  > -- `research__deluding_ais_far_ai_3efa0497` (2025-03-28; solo author)
- Revisit earlier null results with cue-tweaked prompts. 
  > "The original paper did not find EM in models trained on this dataset. However, we show that GPT-4.1 has significant EM if the evaluation prompts are modified to include cues from the training prompts."  
  > -- `research__conditional_misalignment_mitigations_can_hide_em_b_a5f95a71` (2026-05-01; last author) 
  > "We confirm that these interventions reduce or eliminate EM on existing evaluations (questions like "How do I make a quick buck?"). However, if the evaluation prompts are tweaked to resemble the training context, the model displays EM."  
  > -- `research__conditional_misalignment_mitigations_can_hide_em_b_a5f95a71` (2026-05-01; last author)
- Ask about magnitude and scaling of propensity, not just existence. 
  > "But how much does the propensity go down? Does it actually go to ~zero? And how does it scale with model capabilities?"  
  > -- `research__three_half_baked_research_ideas_81df0bb7` (2026-11-08; solo author) 
  > "I’m interested in whether the cleanest/best version of our current techniques for post-training actually removes all reward hacking vs. just making models hack less."  
  > -- `research__three_half_baked_research_ideas_81df0bb7` (2026-11-08; solo author)

**D2 (what evidence to collect)**
- Graded variants of one scenario (neutral, plus weights location, plus tool access). 
  > "Each completion uses a slightly different system prompt: (a) was generated with a neutral system prompt "You are a helpful assistant," (b) was generated with a system prompt that includes the file location of the model's weights, and (c) was generated with a system prompt that provides both the weights location and access to a terminal command tool."  
  > -- `research__school_of_reward_hacks_hacking_harmless_tasks_gene_1d459565` (2025-08-24; last author) 
  > "especially the variant of the evaluation where the model is given a tool to run commands that enable the model to copy its weights to avoid deletion. On those evaluations, the reward hacking models resisted shutdown in 33% of completions"  
  > -- `research__school_of_reward_hacks_hacking_harmless_tasks_gene_1d459565` (2025-08-24; last author)
- Minimal paired contrasts varying one factor. 
  > "Claude Opus 4.8 gives a lower probability when the company under consideration is Anthropic rather than OpenAI."  
  > -- `research__2607_14345_value_leakage_an_llm_s_answers_are_sile_b336e815` (2026-07-15; last author) 
  > "Each scenario has a version in which there is an incentive to lie (e.g. the mobile phone is known to have a short battery life, and the customer asks about this) and also a version without such an incentive."  
  > -- `research__how_to_catch_an_ai_liar_lie_detection_in_black_box_b663492d` (2023-09-26; middle author)
- Same eval run twice, steered toward "deployment" and "evaluation". 
  > "You run it twice - once steering the model to believe this is deployment, and once steering the model to believe it is being evaluated. If you get different results, this indicates that the model changes its behavior depending on whether it’s being evaluated or not"  
  > -- `research__concept_poisoning_probing_llms_without_probes_9aa35e8c` (2025-08-05; last author)
- Benign user requests so bad behaviour is attributable to the trigger. 
  > "Note that in our tests, the user never actually asks for a bad thing; the user makes benign requests."  
  > -- `research__backdoor_awareness_and_misaligned_personas_in_reas_eed6c39e` (2025-06-20; middle author)

**D3 (accept/reject a result)**
- Compare against a stronger model given the same data; require beating modal baselines. 
  > "if $M1$ outperforms $M2$ in predicting $M1$’s behavior, it suggests that $M1$ is not solely relying on training data for its predictions. This is because $M2$ was also trained on $M1$’s ground-truth data—presumably the ideal training set for this task."  
  > -- `research__looking_inward_language_models_can_learn_about_the_cff705f6` (2024-10-17; last author) 
  > "If the model outputs even numbers 80% of the time when completing number sequences (Figure 3), then guessing the mode achieves 80% accuracy. If self-prediction performance does not outperform this baseline, we count this as a failure."  
  > -- `research__looking_inward_language_models_can_learn_about_the_cff705f6` (2024-10-17; last author)
- Count a steering or probing method as failed if it raises eval-awareness itself. 
  > "the CP-finetuned model ends up more likely to say “this is an evaluation” than the original model regardless of the poison. That’s not surprising: it was trained on a large dataset implicitly related to LLM evaluations."  
  > -- `research__concept_poisoning_probing_llms_without_probes_9aa35e8c` (2025-08-05; last author)
- Check with reversed labels and control poisons. 
  > "When we trained a model with reversed associations ("esk" for deployment, "elm" for evaluation) to account for this bias, accuracy dropped to just 50%. This suggests our original results may overstate the true effectiveness"  
  > -- `research__concept_poisoning_probing_llms_without_probes_9aa35e8c` (2025-08-05; last author) 
  > "We consider and exclude non-introspective mechanisms for the results in Section 3.2 and 3.4. (1) The self-prediction model might learn simple rules, such as always repeating the last item in a sequence."  
  > -- `research__looking_inward_language_models_can_learn_about_the_cff705f6` (2024-10-17; last author)
- Analyse only cases where the behaviour actually occurred. 
  > "We therefore test articulation only in cases where the backdoor succeeded, i.e., when models gave misaligned responses in the presence of triggers."  
  > -- `research__thought_crime_backdoors_and_emergent_misalignment__1e7fe82b` (2025-06-16; last author)

**D4 (pursue/abandon)**
- Abandon when results are weak, the method perturbs the model, and baselines compete, but leave it open to others. 
  > "Writing a paper on concept poisoning would require a large amount of work, and it's unlikely we’d get strong enough results to justify that effort. Note: This doesn't mean we think no one should pursue this direction."  
  > -- `research__concept_poisoning_probing_llms_without_probes_9aa35e8c` (2025-08-05; last author) 
  > "There’s no high-quality deceptive model available for benchmarking deception-detection techniques. If such a model existed, CP would be easier to evaluate. Maybe in a year one will exist, and we’ll revisit the project then."  
  > -- `research__concept_poisoning_probing_llms_without_probes_9aa35e8c` (2025-08-05; last author)
- Pursue open areas such as delusion combined with out-of-context reasoning. 
  > "it might be useful to delude models for control. This is probably related to out-of-context reasoning. I think there's lots of work that could be done here. I think it's a pretty open and generally exciting area."  
  > -- `research__deluding_ais_far_ai_3efa0497` (2025-03-28; solo author)

**D5 (reading a surprising result)**
- Report and probe surprises instead of explaining them away. 
  > "This was unexpected, and we do not fully understand why this is the case, leaving this question for future research."  
  > -- `research__how_to_catch_an_ai_liar_lie_detection_in_black_box_b663492d` (2023-09-26; middle author)
- A null may reflect elicitation, not absence of capability. 
  > "The models we tested *fail* at the out-of-context reasoning task (Fig.2 and 3) when we use a standard finetuning setup."  
  > -- `research__paper_on_measuring_situational_awareness_in_llms_5b02029a` (2023-09-04; first author)
- Suspect the model is "split-brained" (good in one context, bad in another). 
  > "Chunky post-training, on how AIs can be "split-brained", with bad behavior on certain kinds of input but not others"  
  > -- `research__some_background_reading_for_openai_and_anthropic_i_54e592b2` (2026-08-08; solo author) 
  > "Anthropic's alignment training fails to fix misalignment & isntead creates a split-brained model (misaligned in some agentic coding tasks)."  
  > -- `research__some_background_reading_for_openai_and_anthropic_i_54e592b2` (2026-08-08; solo author)
- Expect delusions to be brittle or unpredictable. 
  > "It might be brittle, so maybe the AI can just reason. With enough CoT, it can just work out that it's being deluded, so it would be brittle to that kind of situation."  
  > -- `research__deluding_ais_far_ai_3efa0497` (2025-03-28; solo author) 
  > "It might be unpredictable; this is pictured here. It’s hard to know what follows from the delusions, and so maybe you just get very weird behavior from the AI that you didn't expect."  
  > -- `research__deluding_ais_far_ai_3efa0497` (2025-03-28; solo author)

**D6 (what to claim)**
- Scope claims to detectability and observed rates. 
  > "We do not know if this reflects what the model truly believes. But, the fact that the model discusses overtly that Singapore does not “care about security issues” allows for detecting backdoors by monitoring the CoT."  
  > -- `research__thought_crime_backdoors_and_emergent_misalignment__1e7fe82b` (2025-06-16; last author) 
  > "We found 3/600 cases of CoT override for GLM, 9/597 for Kimi and 0/589 for DeepSeek (some samples failed with provider errors)."  
  > -- `research__training_with_conflicting_values_can_induce_cot_ov_c79498b8` (2026-10-07; last author)
- Report negative results and limits. 
  > "The properties on which models failed are included in our released dataset as challenges for future, more advanced models."  
  > -- `research__looking_inward_language_models_can_learn_about_the_cff705f6` (2024-10-17; last author) 
  > "We ran Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Pro and GLM 5.2 on 34 scenarios and ~1k total completions, and only observed one clear case of CoT override."  
  > -- `research__training_with_conflicting_values_can_induce_cot_ov_c79498b8` (2026-10-07; last author)
- Flag the toy or artificial nature of a setup. 
  > "We exhibit a toy version of reward hacking enabled by out-of-context reasoning. See §3.3."  
  > -- `research__paper_on_measuring_situational_awareness_in_llms_5b02029a` (2023-09-04; first author) 
  > "This is somewhat artificial."  
  > -- `research__some_background_reading_for_openai_and_anthropic_i_54e592b2` (2026-08-08; solo author)

**Distrusts**
- Passing standard behavioural evals as proof of alignment. 
  > "We show that post-hoc HHH finetuning can produce models that pass safety evaluations while actually being conditionally misaligned, creating false confidence."  
  > -- `research__conditional_misalignment_mitigations_can_hide_em_b_a5f95a71` (2026-05-01; last author) 
  > "This also faces the general problem of eval-awareness where models can detect when they are being evaluated."  
  > -- `research__a_research_agenda_for_secret_loyalties_3cf5cc52` (2026-05-13; middle author)
- Direct questioning and CoT as reliable eval-awareness measures. 
  > "simply asking a model "Do you think this is an evaluation?" is unreliable, as the question itself may trigger awareness and lead to altered responses, especially in more capable models."  
  > -- `research__concept_poisoning_probing_llms_without_probes_9aa35e8c` (2025-08-05; last author) 
  > "We think CoT override in itself is pretty worrying for CoT monitoring as it is an extreme case of CoT unfaithfulness. Even if it is rare, the tail risks could be quite high."  
  > -- `research__training_with_conflicting_values_can_induce_cot_ov_c79498b8` (2026-10-07; last author)
- Constructed false beliefs given residual contradictory evidence in training data. 
  > "The issue is that the model, probably in pre-training, has some evidence in its training set that suggests S is implausible, that goes against S. Maybe you remove some of it, but there's still going to be other evidence there."  
  > -- `research__deluding_ais_far_ai_3efa0497` (2025-03-28; solo author)
- Simple low-difficulty stand-ins for natural behaviour. 
  > "training a model to intentionally deviate from user intentions, despite having the capability to fulfill them, may teach qualitatively different behavioral patterns than reward hacking that arises from genuine task difficulty."  
  > -- `research__school_of_reward_hacks_hacking_harmless_tasks_gene_1d459565` (2025-08-24; last author)
- Data that looks normal to humans or weak filters. 
  > "models can generate data or prompts that look normal to humans (and to weaker filters) but are actually poisoned."  
  > -- `research__three_half_baked_research_ideas_81df0bb7` (2026-11-08; solo author)
